who_its_for: South African citizens under 35, with at least a 70% average for the last full academic year (for current students); fields include engineering (BSc or BEng, not BTech), IT, computer science, finance, accounting, commerce, data analytics
documents: Certified ID documents of parents or guardians (or death certificates); proof of other bursary or NSFAS funding where applicable; 2027 acceptance letter; for current students certified academic records, matric certificate, 2026 registration proof and fee statement; disability documents (doctor's letter, EEA1) where relevant. All certified documents less than 3 months old.
notes: Closes 12:00 midday on Monday 26 Oct 2026. Administered by Excel@Uni. Work-back obligation; failing the contract conditions can mean repaying with interest. Shortlisted applicants contacted by 31 Jan 2027. No official link found yet: the application portal is run through Excel@Uni. One 2027 listing names only data analytics, chemical engineering and electrical engineering as fields, so the field list may be narrower this year: check the portal.

who_its_for: Students at public universities and TVET colleges who qualify financially
documents: Signed NSFAS consent form, plus forms depending on your situation (declaration form, disability assessment questionnaire, orphan and vulnerable child form). The myNSFAS portal generates your list.
notes: Applications close on 31 October 2026 and NSFAS says there will be no extension (government and NSFAS statements, September to October 2026). The 18 November date mentioned at the launch event was replaced by 31 October. Apply through the myNSFAS portal. Free.

who_its_for: First-year undergraduates in 2027 from households earning R600,000 a year or less, already accepted at a partner university, in selected fields
documents: Signed ISFAP funding application consent form; ID documents of parents, guardians and household earners (certified copies)
notes: Fields and partner universities change yearly. Some students report the portal showing closed. Does not replace NSFAS. Free.

who_its_for: Black South African citizens aged 17 to 21, in matric or having finished first or second year, in eligible fields at recognised institutions
documents: Not captured; listed on the application form
notes: Two sources give 31 Oct 2026, two say no closing date specified. Also see jdkbenefittrust.co.za/how_it_works/.

who_its_for: Students training to teach (BEd) in priority subjects; must teach after graduating; needs a university place
documents: Printed online application plus certified copies of documents (2026 list; check the 2027 one)
notes: Opened 1 Oct 2026. Date shown is for NEW applicants; returning bursars close 30 Nov 2026. Free. Linked to UJ BEd Foundation Phase in source_sheet.csv. The Department of Basic Education page still showed 2026 dates when checked on 24 October 2026, so the 2027 dates come from listings; confirm on eservices.gov.za.

who_its_for: Postgraduate only (Honours, Master's, PhD). South African citizens and permanent residents with at least 65% in their previous degree. Age limits apply: 28 for Honours, 30 for Master's, 32 for PhD.
documents: Documents listed on the official application page
notes: Closing dates differ by level. UNISA's research office lists the NRF call dates as: first-time Master's and Doctoral closed 3 July 2026, and Master's and Doctoral extension support closed 14 August 2026. A November 2026 date for Honours was reported but is not confirmed. Reported: full cost of study for financially needy students (household income up to R350,000 a year) or students with disabilities, and partial cost for other qualifying candidates. Confirm the details on the funder's own page before applying.

who_its_for: Postgraduate only (Postgraduate Diploma, Honours, Master's, Doctoral). Mainly South African citizens registered at UNISA. Students moving from an undergraduate degree into Honours need a 60% average.
documents: Documents listed on the official application page
notes: UNISA's page says the 2027 postgraduate bursary application period runs from 21 September to 30 November 2026. The funding is for UNISA students, and Master's and doctoral funding has research-stage requirements, so read the UNISA guidelines. Reported: tuition fees for Postgraduate Diploma and Honours students; Master's and doctoral students may also get research allowances. Confirm the details on the funder's own page before applying.

who_its_for: Postgraduate only (Honours and postgraduate CTA). Unemployed South African citizens with financial need, studying Law, Mathematics, Statistics, Actuarial Science or Accounting.
documents: Documents listed on the official application page
notes: Applications for 2027 closed on 30 September 2026 (IDC advert shared by NWU and several listings). Do not apply unless the IDC announces a reopening. Reported limits: household income up to R350,000 a year and age 26 or younger. The scheme mainly funds a first qualification. Reported: tuition, accommodation, meals, transport and a once-off laptop allowance. Confirm the details on the funder's own page before applying.

who_its_for: Postgraduate only (Honours, Master's, Doctoral). South African citizens studying relevant science and engineering qualifications, with an average of at least 65%.
documents: Documents listed on the official application page
notes: Reported: fixed yearly funding limits that differ by level (Honours, Master's, Doctoral). Details come from a summary and have not been checked against the funder's own page yet; confirm the closing date and rules before applying. SANSA's usual cycle is 1 to 31 October for the next year of study, and 31 October 2026 is the expected 2027 closing date, but it is not confirmed.

who_its_for: Postgraduate only (Master's and PhD). Nationals of eligible Southern African countries studying in South Africa, in justice (climate justice, law, economics, politics), education policy or humanities.
documents: Documents listed on the official application page
notes: Stage 1 for 2027 has closed. The Canon Collins page text gives 14 August 2026 at 16:00, and some listings report an extension to 21 August 2026 at 16:00 SAST. Stage 2 is by invitation only. Reported: support for up to two years, with the option to reapply for a third year depending on performance. Watch for the next call. Confirm the details on the funder's own page before applying.

who_its_for: Postgraduate only (first postgraduate degree). South African citizens accepted at an ISFAP partner university who meet the academic and financial requirements set by the donors.
documents: Documents listed on the official application page
notes: Reported: a full package covering tuition, accommodation, a monthly living allowance and student support. This is separate from the undergraduate ISFAP bursary above. Details come from a summary and have not been checked against the funder's own page yet; confirm the closing date and rules before applying. A listing reports 31 October 2026 for selected programmes, but ISFAP funding is programme and university specific, so check your own programme on the portal.
